title: WHEN THE PICTURE MUST BE PERFECT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD said to Moses, 'Say to Aaron: "For the generations to come
none of your descendants who has a defect may come near to offer the
food of his God"'" - Lev 21:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now we come to one of the hardest sections of the chapter. A
descendant of Aaron with a physical defect could not serve at the
altar. To modern ears this sounds unfair, even cruel. Let us handle it
honestly.

First, this was never a statement about a person's value. Scripture is
clear that God does not see as man sees (1 Sam 16:7). It was also not
about salvation or God's love.

Second, everything in the tabernacle was a picture. The animals had to
be without blemish. The furnishings had to be exact. The priests had
to be physically whole. Nothing in that system was allowed to suggest
imperfection, because the whole arrangement was pointing forward to
One who would be perfect in every way.

Third, and most importantly, the picture has now been replaced by the
reality. Jesus is the truly unblemished One (1 Pet 1:19). And because
of Him, the barriers came down. The very people the old system kept at
a distance were the ones Jesus drew near - the blind, the lame, the
outcast.

Dear reader, in Christ no physical condition keeps you from God's
presence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I ever feel too flawed to come near to God?
2. How does Christ's perfection give me confidence to approach the
   Father?
3. Does my church welcome those the world sidelines?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Christ's perfection, not mine, opens the way to
You. Help me never make anyone feel unwelcome in Your presence. Amen.
